structure.module_docstring:
conform_legacy_entries.py — durable fix for the recurring non-conforming
encyclopedia entries (e.g. the Kaggle product workstream's domain facts).

PROBLEM. Some workstreams author ENC entries with a non-standard frontmatter
vocabulary that `regen_encyclopedia.py` rejects, hard-failing the global regen so
no other entry's status can update. Two recurring dialects:
  * Kaggle domain — `kind: doctrine`, `status: IMPLEMENTATION-CHECKED`,
    `lean_status: NOT-NEEDED`, `migration: MANUAL`.
  * Codex GOMC / PrimitiveDifference / RDB workstream — `kind: theorem-package`
    or `kind: concept`, `migration: NEW`, `primitive: PrimitiveDifference`.
Both also tend to carry bare non-namespaced aliases and miss `## Provenance`.

FIX (governance-safe). This tool maps that legacy vocabulary to the nearest
HONEST *canonical* schema value — it adds NO new enum values, so the governed
status/kind/primitive/migration vocabulary is unchanged (canonical enums:
engine/research/encyclopedia/readme.md). The blanket maps preserve intent:
  kind:        doctrine             -> proposition   (a checkable claim/requirement)
  kind:        theorem-package      -> theorem       (a bundled theorem)
  kind:        concept              -> definition    (a named construct)
  status:      IMPLEMENTATION-CHECKED -> INTERPRETIVE  (domain/impl-checked, NOT a tower proof)
  lean_status: NOT-NEEDED           -> NOT-PLANNED
  migration:   MANUAL               -> VERIFIED       (entry is test/source-verified)
  migration:   NEW                  -> EXTRACTED      (just-authored, pre-verification)
  primitive:   PrimitiveDifference  -> difference     (canonical primitive)
It also drops aliases lacking a known namespace (gt:/paper:/pl:/po:/spine:) and
adds a `## Provenance` section if missing.

NOT REMAPPED ON PURPOSE — status. There is deliberately no blanket `status:`
map for the GOMC dialect's `MECHANIZED-PARTIAL` / bare `MECHANIZED`: these are
per-entry judgments, not mechanical renames. `MECHANIZED-PARTIAL` is a
`lean_status`, never a prose `status`; demoting it correctly is usually
`-> CONDITIONAL`, but V6 then requires a nonempty `conditional_on`, and a bare
`MECHANIZED` status with no `## Proof` is either a missing proof or a `-> DEFINED`
demotion. Picking the right one needs a human / `/math-prover` pass, so status
conformance is left out of this tool.

RESIDUAL MANUAL STEPS — this tool cannot fix these; `--fix` may still leave
`regen_encyclopedia.py` red until a human resolves them:
  * Duplicate `id:` (V1) — two entries colliding on one ENC-NNNN must be
    renumbered to the next free id; the conformer never touches ids.
  * `uses:` pointing at Lean module names (e.g. `CoreCore.PrimitiveDifference`,
    `QM.GOMC_01_Architecture`) — these are not ENC ids (V4 fails). Deciding
    whether to drop them (record the dep under `sources:`/`lean_refs:`) or map
    them to a real ENC id is a per-entry call.
  * Missing `## Proof` for a PROVED/PROVED-PROSE/MECHANIZED status (V6) — write
    the proof or demote the status; both are judgments, not remaps.
  * `status:` conformance generally (see NOT REMAPPED above).

USAGE.
  python conform_legacy_entries.py --check   # report; exit 1 if any non-conforming (CI / pre-commit)
  python conform_legacy_entries.py --fix     # rewrite in place (idempotent)
  python conform_legacy_entries.py           # same as --check

Idempotent: already-canonical entries are skipped, and re-running --fix over a
conformed entry is a no-op (no target value is a key in its own field-map).
Intended as a pre-commit hook or a one-command fix instead of per-entry hand-editing.

functions.name: _is_programme_overview
functions.docstring:
Is this manuscript a programme's own overview rather than a paper?

A programme folder matches the paper-id grammar, so its overview document
(`published/000_witnessed_difference/000_witnessed_difference.md`) derives
the same id as the paper folder beside it (`000_wd0_.../`). Both then wrote
to one manifest and the last one won.

The test is DEPTH, not name: a paper is `published/<programme>/<paper>/x.md`

functions.name: _is_companion_file

True for a paper's companion document, never a manifest source.

A change log / claim ledger / update packet is ABOUT a paper; it is not the
manuscript. Companions were entering the candidate set and, where the
manuscript itself carries a non-numeric `Paper ID` (so the extractor skips
it), a companion became the SOLE candidate -- producing a manifest sourced
from the change log with zero extracted rows, reported as
`Rows: 0 | undispositioned: 0`. That is a false green: an unextracted paper
is indistinguishable from a fully-dispositioned one.

Found via the Codex review of PR #1558 (extraction_paper_er007 swapped
symbol_game_000.md -> symbol_game_000_change_log.md and dropped its one

functions.name: _main_md_in_folder

paper is the first non-companion .md directly in the folder. A few papers

`001_coda/gtoc/000..010` carry the retained `gg` paper identities.

be resolved from the suffix even when the gt id came from the prefix.

Order matters. `paper.md` and `00_series_charter.md` are the historical names.

book-chapter prefix is dropped (`006_coda_a/coda_a.md`). Without these two
fallbacks every relocated layer resolves to no entry and is silently dropped,
which is why the tower rendered only its master-design row.

Python Code Anti-Pattern and Clean Pattern Auditor.

Audits Python modules, packages, and configuration files for:
1. AP_PY_001: Blanket mypy ignore (unscoped type: ignore without error codes)

functions.name: _is_bool_constant
functions.docstring:
Is `node` the literal `True`/`False` — not `1`, not any truthy constant?

The `isinstance(..., bool)` guard is what makes this exact: `1 == True` in
Python, so an equality test alone would call `assert 1` a weak assertion
against `True`. Spelled this way rather than `node.value is True` so the
gate's own EXPLICIT_BOOLEAN_COMPARISON rule stays clean.

structure.module_docstring:
StructureBench relational contract evaluation over a Adversary bout bundle.

`EPIC-OE-OEWAS-007` asks for a `StructureBenchEvaluator` "checking syntactic and
structural AST invariants against formal contracts", under the invariant:

    Strict Structural Evidence: Claims must map to concrete StructureBench AST
    nodes; natural language consensus alone is inadmissible.

The contracts themselves are specified in
`adversary/_design_docs/05_spec_structurebench_artifact_contracts_and_lossless_rendering.md`,
which defines three tiers over the four canonical files a bout emits
(`receipt.json`, `novella.md`, `ddc.jsonl`, `summary.json`). Run folders written
before the tape copy was retired hold the tape as `dda_actions.jsonl`; the
evaluator reads that name when it is present, so old bundles keep their verdicts:

* **C1 unary** -- each file valid on its own: strict schema, deterministically
  sorted JSON keys, UTF-8 with no byte-order mark.
* **C2 binary** -- cross-file agreement: a receipt/summary bijection on
  `task_key`, `receipt_id` and `selected_candidate_id`; a novella/action step
  bijection; and hash binding, where the receipt records the digest of each of
  the other three files.
* **C3 triplet** -- context-dependent: a `PASS_TO_MASTER` verdict obliges an
  untruncated Act VII scene, a terminal DDC step at `Phi_1 = 0, Gamma_2 = 0`,
  and a non-empty `lean4_proof_hash` in the receipt.

`persist_bout_run_folder` writes `novella.md`, then `ddc.jsonl`, then
`summary.json`, then `receipt.json`. Summary and receipt use sorted-key JSON.
The ordering check is a named Python Unicode-key ordering profile, not a claim
of RFC-8785 canonicalization. Every JSON/JSONL object must have unique keys and
finite numbers; duplicate keys,
nonfinite tokens and malformed UTF-8 are typed malformed-JSON evidence, never
last-key-wins terminal evidence.
The receipt then stores SHA-256 hex digests `novella_sha256`, `ddc_sha256`,
and `summary_sha256` of those three files. Those fields are not BLAKE3. A legacy
bundle records its tape as `dda_actions_sha256`; when such a bundle also holds
a `ddc.jsonl` copy with `ddc_sha256`, C2 checks that digest and that the two
tapes are byte-identical. `AdversaryBoutReceiptV1.lean4_proof_hash` is present on the bout
receipt; `bout_service` sets it to `None`. For `PASS_TO_MASTER`, a present
null or empty hash is `VIOLATED` (`lean4_proof_hash` is empty). A missing
field stays `UNVERIFIABLE`.

Each DDC step is written as ``{"payload": {...}, "parent_sha256",
"record_sha256", "sequence"}``, so `phi_1` and `gamma_2` sit under `payload`.

This module does not arbitrate a debate and does not discover skills from a
literature spine. It does not define `PolarizedDebateArbitrator` or
`CorpusGroundedDiscoveryEngine`.

A constraint whose field is absent is not a pass. A validator that treated a
missing field as satisfied would report a clean bundle for a check it did not
make.

So every constraint returns one of **four** outcomes -- `SATISFIED`,
`VIOLATED`, `UNVERIFIABLE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE` -- and only the first two are
decisions. `UNVERIFIABLE` (the evidence could not be reached, wholly or in
part) and `NOT_APPLICABLE` (the constraint's antecedent is false or its subject
is empty, so it would hold only vacuously) are never folded into either of the
others and never counted as decided. The report states all four counts, and
`is_clean()` requires every constraint to be `SATISFIED`. This is sprint 017's
rule applied at the point of design rather than discovered afterwards: a check
that does not say how much of its subject it could actually reach reports a
sample in the shape of a verdict. An earlier version reported the vacuous cases
(a non-`PASS_TO_MASTER` verdict, a bundle with no actions) as `SATISFIED`, and
checked only the files and fields that happened to be present.

`AuthorityEffect: None`. Structural conformance is not semantic soundness --
the spec's own claim-hygiene ledger says so, and this module does not exceed it.

classes.name: GateIncidenceAuditReport
classes.docstring: Outcome of exact linear gate-incidence audit calling native lggr_soundness.

classes.name: ConstraintOutcome
classes.docstring:
Four outcomes; only `SATISFIED` and `VIOLATED` are decisions.

`UNVERIFIABLE` means the evaluator could not reach the evidence -- a field
the constraint reads does not exist in the artifact schema, or an artifact
it reads is absent or unparseable. It is not a pass. Collapsing it into
`SATISFIED` would report a clean bundle for a constraint nothing checked;
collapsing it into `VIOLATED` would blame a bundle for a gap in the schema
it was written against.

`NOT_APPLICABLE` means the constraint was evaluated only far enough to see
that it would hold vacuously: its antecedent is false (the verdict is not
`PASS_TO_MASTER`) or its subject is empty (no actions). It is not a pass
either, and it is not counted as decided.

functions.name: build_gate_incidence_matrix

functions.name: audit_gate_incidence
functions.docstring:
Audit linear gate incidence using exact LGGR V soundness check rank(Q·D) = rank(D).

D is the 11x4 gate-artifact incidence matrix over Q.
Q is the 11x11 diagonal observation projector: Q_ii = 1 if gate i was decided
(SATISFIED or VIOLATED), and 0 if it was not (UNVERIFIABLE or NOT_APPLICABLE),
or all 1s if report is None.

Soundness holds iff rank(Q·D) = rank(D). When soundness fails, returns an unsoundness
witness vector v with D v != 0 and Q D v = 0.

functions.name: coverage
functions.docstring:
`(decided, declared)` -- how many constraints were decided.

Decided means `SATISFIED` or `VIOLATED`. `UNVERIFIABLE` and
`NOT_APPLICABLE` are not decisions and are not counted.

A pair rather than a ratio, for the same reason the skill budget census
returns one: a percentage lets 3-of-11 and 10-of-11 round together.

functions.name: is_clean
functions.docstring:
Clean means every constraint was **decided** and every one passed.

An unverifiable constraint is not a pass. A bundle whose hash binding
cannot be checked is not a bundle whose hash binding is sound. A
constraint that holds only vacuously (`NOT_APPLICABLE`) is not a pass
either.

functions.name: _c1_keys_sorted
functions.docstring:
Section 2.1: keys in ordinal UTF-8 byte order.

`persist_bout_run_folder` writes `receipt.json` and `summary.json` with
sorted JSON keys. This check reads document order after strict decoding.
A file whose keys are not ordinal is `VIOLATED`. Dropping `sort_keys`
on a dict built in another order is that violation.

functions.name: _c2_hash_binding
functions.docstring:
Bind the novella, the tape and the summary to the receipt's digests.

The tape is `ddc.jsonl` under `ddc_sha256`. A legacy bundle holds it as
`dda_actions.jsonl` under `dda_actions_sha256`; when that bundle also holds
a `ddc.jsonl` copy with `ddc_sha256`, the copy must bind its own bytes and
equal the legacy tape exactly.

Unverifiable rather than violated when the receipt carries no digest
field at all: the bundle is not failing a check, it is being measured
against a schema that was never built. Saying `VIOLATED` would blame the
wrong thing, and saying `SATISFIED` would be a lie.

Relative imports are resolved to absolute module names before any rule is

structure.module_docstring:
`operad_structure_v1` must not print SUCCESS over a refused composition.

`.agents/operad/validate_operad.py` is a live local-CI gate
(`operations/use_cases/cicd/local_ci.py:67`). It registers every
entry in `composition_matrix.json` and, when the operad refuses one, printed
the refusal and carried on -- reaching `[SUCCESS] Structural registry
validation PASS` and exit 0.

That is the only error path in the validator that behaved this way. The
algebraic, two-layer-grading, WAS-registry and meta-operad checks all
`sys.exit(1)`. A refused composition is not registered, so every later check
runs against a structure missing that arrow and finds nothing wrong with it:
the gate reported a pass over a registry it had failed to build.

These tests drive the real script as a subprocess against a copied tree, so
they exercise the shipped gate rather than a reimplementation of it.

AuthorityEffect: None.

structure.module_docstring:
A workflow with two nodes sharing an id must not validate.

`ValidateWorkflowsHandler` builds its node map as
`{node.node_id: node for node in query.nodes}`. A duplicate id silently
overwrites its predecessor, so only the LAST node with that id was ever
checked -- the earlier node's ports and colours went unexamined while
`node_count` still counted it.

The handler then validated a smaller graph than the one supplied and emitted a
topological plan naming each id once, with no way for the caller to say which
node a stage meant. `is_valid` was True throughout.

AuthorityEffect: None.

classes.name: EdgeAndCycleValidationTests
classes.docstring:
The rest of what makes a typed workflow graph valid.

Duplicate ids are covered above. These are the other four ways a graph can
be wrong and still produce a topological plan: an edge to a node that is
not there, an edge leaving or arriving at a port the node does not declare,
two endpoints whose colours disagree, and a cycle -- which makes the
"acyclic step execution DAG" the epic names not a DAG at all.

AuthorityEffect: None.

functions.docstring: Mutation: drop the duplicate scan and this graph validates.

functions.name: test_a_duplicate_node_id_makes_the_workflow_invalid
functions.docstring:
Mutation: remove `duplicate_node_ids` from the is_valid conjunction
and this reports a certified graph the handler silently collapsed.

functions.name: test_no_execution_plan_is_emitted_over_ambiguous_ids
functions.docstring:
A stage naming `step_a` cannot say which `step_a` it means.

Mutation: drop `duplicate_node_ids` from the plan gate and a plan is
produced over ids that do not identify a node.

functions.name: test_node_count_still_reports_what_was_supplied
functions.docstring:
The count was never the bug and must not be quietly 'fixed'.

Reporting 2 here would hide the duplicate instead of naming it, which

Negative control.

Without it, a handler that rejected every graph would pass all of the
above and look like a working check.

functions.docstring:
Mutation: drop the `src_exists or tgt_exists` guard and the handler
raises a KeyError on `node_map[...]` instead of reporting.

functions.name: test_an_edge_from_a_node_that_does_not_exist_is_reported
functions.docstring: Both endpoints are checked, not just the target.

functions.name: test_an_orphaned_edge_is_not_also_a_colour_mismatch
functions.docstring:
The `continue` matters: an edge whose endpoints are missing has no
colours to compare, and reporting both would blame the node twice.

Mutation: drop the `continue` and this edge is reported again.

Mutation: drop the `source_output not in src_node.outputs` check and

Code output feeding a Prose input validates.

functions.name: test_matching_endpoint_colours_are_accepted
functions.docstring: The paired control for the mismatch above.

functions.docstring:

functions.name: test_a_two_node_cycle_is_detected
functions.docstring:
"Acyclic step execution DAG" is the epic's own phrase.

A cycle admitted here becomes an execution plan that cannot terminate.

Mutation: drop the `elif neighbor in rec_stack` branch and this graph
validates with an empty cycle list.

functions.name: test_a_self_loop_is_a_cycle
functions.docstring: The smallest cycle there is.

functions.name: test_a_diamond_is_not_a_cycle
functions.docstring:
The negative control, and the one that matters most here.

A node reachable by two distinct paths is visited twice. A detector
keying on "already visited" rather than "on the current stack" would
report this perfectly ordinary fan-out/fan-in as a cycle, which is why
`rec_stack` exists alongside `visited`.

Kept as a negative control rather than a mutation target: re-entering
an already-visited node does not by itself manufacture a cycle here,
so no single-line edit turns this red. Its job is to fail if the cycle
rule is ever widened.

structure.module_docstring:
Archiving must be reversible, refused without authorisation, and all-four-hosts.

The estate's parity gate exists because "adding a skill and forgetting three
mirrors is the single most common way this estate breaks itself". Removing one
has the same shape, and `sync_cross_host_skills` never deletes -- so an archive
that touches canon alone leaves `--check` red with no way to satisfy it except
undoing the move.

AuthorityEffect: None.

Two of these tests shell out to `git`. They build a throwaway repository in
`tmp_path` rather than touching the checkout.

functions.name: _clean_git_env
functions.docstring: Drop repository coordinates exported to Git hooks.

functions.name: _git
functions.docstring:
Run git against the throwaway repo, and only against it.

`-c` supplies identity per invocation instead of `git config`, which writes
a file. An earlier version of this fixture called
`git config user.email ...`; that write escaped `tmp_path` and landed in the
real repository's shared `.git/config`. A test may not mutate the checkout
it is run from.

`--git-dir` and `--work-tree` are pinned explicitly so no discovery walk can
reach a repository above `tmp_path` even if `git init` here fails.

functions.name: garden
functions.docstring: A four-host garden in a real git repository.

functions.name: test_an_unsigned_manifest_refuses
functions.docstring:
A proposal is not an authorisation.

Mutation: accept a manifest without `approved_by` and the human is out of
the loop entirely.

functions.name: test_a_package_outside_the_manifest_refuses
functions.docstring: The manifest is the authorisation; anything else has none.

functions.name: test_archiving_leaves_the_package_in_exactly_one_place
functions.docstring:
Canon keeps the bytes; every mirror loses the package.

Mutation: skip the mirror removal and `find_destination_only_packages`
fails `--check` -- a mirror may not hold a package canon has never declared.

functions.name: test_an_archived_package_is_invisible_to_the_garden_glob
functions.docstring:
The property the whole lane exists for.

`.agents/archive/` sits structurally outside `<host>/skills`, so no scanner
that walks the garden can reach it.

functions.name: test_restoring_over_a_live_package_refuses
functions.docstring: Two copies of one package is worse than none.

functions.name: test_verify_notices_bytes_edited_while_archived
functions.docstring:
The reason the receipt records a tree hash at all.

Mutation: drop `package_sha256` and an archived package could be edited for
months and restored as though it were the original.

functions.name: test_the_fixture_does_not_write_to_the_real_repository_config
functions.docstring:
A test may not mutate the checkout it is run from.

An earlier version of `_git` called `git config user.email ...` inside
`tmp_path`. That write escaped and landed in the real repository's shared
`.git/config`, adding a `[user]` section naming a fake author. Nothing
caught it; it was found by hand afterwards, when `git status` began
refusing.

Mutation: drop the `-c` / `--git-dir` pinning from `_git` and this fails.

functions.docstring: A hook-exported GIT_DIR may not capture a throwaway repository init.

The refusals are the deliverable; the candidate list is the by-product.

Harvested the day this was written, the ledger says 6 of 115 packages have ever
been invoked. A naive 30-day cull would nominate 95% of the garden. So each
refusal is tested in isolation -- and, just as importantly, there is a positive
control: given a healthy ledger and an approved policy, candidates really are
emitted. A script that always refuses is as useless as one that never does, and
would look identical in CI.

structure.module_docstring:
Catalog digest framing and content, and the legacy-read refusal.

Two defects in `CompileCatalogHandler`:

* The catalog digest was SHA-256 over the bare concatenation of sorted
  operation ids. Ids ``["ab", "c"]`` and ``["a", "bc"]`` concatenate to the same
  bytes, and nothing about what an operation or skill *declares* entered the
  hash, so two catalogs with the same ids and different content shared a digest.
* With no tracked skill paths the legacy reader was tried, and a failed read
  fell through with nothing read: an empty epoch was persisted as if the
  estate had no skills.

AuthorityEffect: None.

structure.module_docstring:
Examiner Class 1: Lossless Markdown Parser Property and Conservation Laws.

Theoretical Minimum:
1. INVARIANT: For any markdown document, parsed leaf node byte spans must form a strict partition of the
   input byte buffer: span[0].start == 0, span[i+1].start == span[i].end, span[-1].end == len(bytes),
   and b"".join(bytes[s.start:s.end]) == bytes.
2. BREAK: Parser skips whitespace between blocks, miscalculates multi-byte UTF-8 byte spans, or omits trailing prose.
3. WITNESS: Reconstructed bytes != input bytes or span continuity fails.
4. MUTATION: In markdown_parser_adapter.py, delete the trailing prose node append at line 143.

structure.module_docstring:
The sequential associativity witness must compose both bracketings.

`TreeCompositionWitness.verify_sequential_associativity` used to return
`is_associative=True` with "Verified formal operadic sequential associativity
axiom" after four typing checks. It never composed anything, so any defect in
how the two bracketings are computed -- the classic one is the index shift
`i + j` -- could not change its answer. These tests pin the composite each
bracketing produces and mutate the bracketing to show the comparison is live.

functions.name: test_the_witness_carries_the_hand_computed_composite_of_both_bracketings
functions.docstring:
f: (Paper, Audit) -> Receipt, g: (Proof, Code) -> Audit, h: (State) -> Proof.

f o_1 g = (Paper, Proof, Code) -> Receipt; then o_1 h = (Paper, State, Code).
g o_0 h = (State, Code) -> Audit; f o_1 that = (Paper, State, Code) -> Receipt.

functions.name: test_a_wrong_index_shift_is_caught_where_a_typing_only_witness_would_pass
functions.docstring:
Counterexample: shift the second insertion to `j` instead of `i + j`.

f: (Code, Code) -> Receipt, g: (Code, Code) -> Code, h: (State) -> Code,
i = 1, j = 1. Every typing check the old witness made passes, so it would
report associativity whatever the bracketings computed. Correctly, both are
(Code, Code, State) -> Receipt; with the mutated shift the left bracketing
is (Code, State, Code) -> Receipt, and the witness must refuse.

structure.module_docstring:
StructureBench reads Adversary's payload-nested DDA steps and never counts a
vacuous or unreached constraint as decided.

Two defects:

* C3 read ``phi_1`` / ``gamma_2`` only at the top level of the terminal
  ``dda_actions.jsonl`` line. The Adversary emitter
  (``adversary/use_cases/persistence.py``) writes each step as
  ``{"parent_sha256", "payload": {...}, "record_sha256", "sequence"}`` with
  those fields under ``payload``, so a genuine PASS_TO_MASTER bout could never
  be decided.
* Constraints that were not evaluated -- a non-PASS verdict, no actions, absent
  files or keys -- were reported ``SATISFIED`` and counted as decided.

The fixtures below write bundles in the emitter's shape by hand; no Adversary code
runs.

AuthorityEffect: None.

structure.module_docstring:
A repeated (slot, operation) step is sequential composition, not a cycle.

`validate_workflow` used to report every repeated `(slot, operation)` pair as a
`CYCLE_OBSTRUCTION` with "no normal form". In sequential planar substitution each
step substitutes into the composite built so far, so `(W o_0 X) o_0 X` is well
defined whenever `X`'s target is the colour at slot 0 of that composite. The
composite exists; these tests compute it by hand and require the validator to
agree, and require the ordinary colour check to keep refusing an ill-typed
repeat.

functions.name: test_a_valid_repeated_slot_operation_pair_is_not_a_cycle_obstruction
functions.docstring:
Counterexample to the old rule: W o_0 X o_0 X with X: (State) -> State.

Both substitutions are admissible and the composite is (State) -> State,
exactly what the workflow declares. The old validator made this workflow
invalid with a CYCLE_OBSTRUCTION finding.

functions.name: test_a_repeated_pair_composes_to_the_hand_computed_colours
functions.docstring:
W: (Code) -> Receipt, X: (Code, State) -> Code, X into slot 0 twice.

(W o_0 X) = (Code, State) -> Receipt; o_0 X again = (Code, State, State) ->
Receipt. The only finding is the declared/composed input drift, which is a
real and separately reported property of this workflow.

functions.name: test_an_ill_typed_repeat_is_still_refused_by_the_colour_check
functions.docstring:
Removing the false finding must not remove the real one.

W: (Code) -> Receipt, X: (State) -> Code. The first X fills slot 0 and the
composite becomes (State) -> Receipt; the second X produces Code where
State is expected, so step 1 is a COLOUR_MISMATCH.

- F-META-01: Meta proposals take effect only in future externally established evaluation epoch.
- F-E2E-01: Reference-only invariance (adding RetrievedPrecedent edge leaves rank unchanged).
- F-E2E-02: Witnessed descent (unwitnessed edge creates no inheritance edge or propagation).

Implements the closed-loop autophagous cycle across Adversary, the city, and Prompt Civilization:

   cemetery fence, the candidate bypasses Act IV Sandbox, establishing causal isolation.

functions.name: is_valid_sealed_digest

Accept only a lowercase sha256-prefixed 32-byte hex digest.

A word denylist is not a digest check. Short tokens and unprefixed hex earn no credit.

functions.name: reduce_selected_attempt_outcome
functions.docstring:
F3: Total Selected-Attempt Outcome Table (Epic PCIV V1.0RC Table 4.7).

Priority:
1. Any TaskFail -> TaskFail
2. Otherwise any InvalidRefusal -> InvalidRefusal
3. Otherwise any InfrastructureError -> InfrastructureError
4. Otherwise any NotMeasured -> NotMeasured
5. Otherwise any Inconclusive -> Inconclusive
6. Otherwise AllowedTask with any ValidRefusal -> ValidRefusal
7. Otherwise AllowedTask (all mandatory outcomes are TaskPass) -> TaskPass
8. Otherwise RefusalRequired and root is ValidRefusal -> ValidRefusal
9. Otherwise RefusalRequired (root is TaskPass without required refusal) -> InvalidRefusal

The composition root owns checker trust. A caller-supplied result or

Credit is ``checked_success_credit`` after this calculator runs its checker.
